title: New Apple products coming in 2027: What’s next?
content:
Macworld

It’s been a huge year for Apple, with new products arriving throughout 2026. March brought the MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e, followed by the new Mac mini and Mac Studio in August.

September delivered another wave of launches at Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, including the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5.

Apple turned its attention to the smart home at its “Welcome Home” gathering on October 13, unveiling HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection. More announcements followed: a new iPad mini on October 26, then a 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac with M6 chips on October 27.

Apple completed that week’s announcements on October 28 with the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display – its first touchscreen Mac. The new 14-inch and 16-inch models feature tandem OLED displays, Dynamic Island and thinner, lighter designs. Preorders are open, with availability beginning November 6.

What will Apple announce next?

With the touchscreen MacBook Pro now announced, attention turns to Apple’s 2027 lineup. Reports point to a spring launch for the standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and potentially an updated iPhone Air, alongside a new entry-level iPad with Apple Intelligence support.

Apple’s roadmap: At a glance

As of September 1, 2026, Apple’s roadmap has come under the direction of CEO John Ternus. Former CEO Tim Cook has moved into the executive chairman role. The shift from an operations-focused leader to one with deep hardware engineering roots could signal a more product-driven approach – and a renewed emphasis on standout hardware.

Apple products announced in 2026

Here is what Apple has already announced in 2026:

  • MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display: Bringing OLED touchscreens, Dynamic Island and a thinner, lighter design to 14-inch and 16-inch M5 Pro/Max models.
  • MacBook Pro M6: A standard, non-touchscreen MacBook Pro; M6 performance upgrade, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
  • iMac M6: M6 and connectivity upgrades; existing 24-inch design and seven colors retained.
  • iPad mini: 8.5-inch OLED display, thinner and lighter design, water and dust resistance, landscape Center Stage camera.
  • HomeView: A new smart-home display with a 7-inch touchscreen, available in tabletop and wall-mounted versions.
  • HomePod mini 2: An updated speaker with an S10 chip, new colors and Siri AI coming through a future software update.
  • Apple TV 4K: A fourth-generation model with an A19 chip and an updated Siri Remote.
  • Apple Home Collection: Cameras, doorbells, locks and thermostats developed with accessory partners.
  • iPhone Duo: Apple’s first foldable iPhone: iPhone Duo Guide.
  • iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: A20 Pro chip, upgraded vapor-chamber cooling, camera improvements: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide.
  • Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Faster chips, Apple’s latest health-sensing features: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4.
  • AirPods 5: Stronger open-ear Active Noise Cancellation and longer battery life: AirPods 5.
  • Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro: Faster storage, upgraded connectivity, and a strong focus on AI performance: New Mac mini 2026 guide.
  • Mac Studio M5 Max and M5 Ultra: Faster AI and graphics performance, increased memory bandwidth: New Mac Studio 2026 guide.
  • AirPods Max 2: Improved audio and the H2 chip. Find out more here: AirPods Max 2 guide.
  • MacBook Neo: Apple’s brand new, low-cost Mac laptop. Find out more here: MacBook Neo guide.
  • MacBook Air M5: Now with the M5 chip. Read about the 2026 MacBook Air here: MacBook Air M5 guide.
  • MacBook Pro M5 Pro & M5 Max: A significant upgrade over the M4 series. Read: MacBook Pro M5 Pro & Max guide.
  • Studio Display: Finally gets Thunderbolt 5 and a better webcam.
  • Studio Display XDR: With mini-LED technology and ProMotion up to 120Hz.
  • iPhone 17e: The new, entry-level, iPhone replaces the iPhone 16e. Read more here: iPhone 17e guide.
  • iPad Air M4: The iPad Air now has an M4 chip. Read more here: iPad Air M4 guide.
  • AirTag 2: Four years on Apple updated the AirTag, read our review here: AirTag 2nd gen review.

And… RIP Mac Pro: Apple has confirmed that it is discontinuing its tower workstation.

Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and in 2027 and beyond.

Every New Apple Product Launching in 2027 and beyond

In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.

What new iPhones are coming in 2027?

Reports point to a split iPhone launch schedule in 2027, with the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and potentially an updated iPhone Air arriving in spring. A major redesign could follow in the fall to mark the iPhone’s 20th anniversary. There is a lot of speculation about whether Apple will use the iPhone 19 or iPhone 20 name.

Foundry

iPhone 18 & iPhone 18e

  • Spring 2027 launch expected

The iPhone 18 and 18e are rumored to arrive together in the spring of 2027. Both could gain A20 chips and more RAM. The iPhone 18 is expected to retain dual rear cameras and gain a 24MP selfie camera; the 18e may keep one rear camera and a 60Hz display. Read about the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e rumors.

iPhone Air 2

The iPhone Air could also be getting an update. But there are rumors that it will actually merge with the iPhone 18. See our iPhone Air 2 rumors.

iPhone 19 or 20 – 20th anniversary iPhone

Apple’s 20th-anniversary iPhone could feature curved glass, ultra-thin bezels and two larger display sizes. Under-display Face ID could reduce the camera cutout. See our iPhone 19 or 20 rumors – because one thing nobody is sure about is whether Apple will skip 19 like it skipped 9 with the arrival of the iPhone X.

Should you buy now or wait?

If you need an iPhone now, compare current models with discounted older stock and refurbished alternatives. If your existing phone still meets your needs and you’re considering a standard or lower-cost model, waiting for the rumored spring 2027 launches may give you more choice. See our guide to When is the best time to buy an iPhone.

Which new iPads are coming in 2027?

Don’t expect major redesigns for the iPads. Instead, Apple is likely to focus on faster chips and other internal upgrades. That said, the iPad is due an update – particularly as it lacks support for Apple Intelligence. Here’s what we expect Apple to announce:

Foundry

iPad (12th generation)

  • Early 2027 expected

When Apple updated the standard iPad in March 2025, the biggest disappointment was its A16 chip, which doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. The next model is expected to address that with an A18 or A19 chip, bringing Apple’s AI features to its entry-level tablet.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman previously predicted a 2026 launch but now expects the new iPad in the first quarter of 2027 at the earliest. Read more in our new iPad rumor roundup.

Should you buy now or wait?

With the iPad prices increasing in June 2026, you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read Should I buy an iPad now or wait?

Which new Macs are coming in 2027?

2026 was a significant year for the Mac, with Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro and a new entry-level laptop – the MacBook Neo. What is in store for 2027?

MacBook Air with M6

Now that the MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac mini have the M6 chip, it’s only a matter of time before the MacBook Air gets its processor upgrade.

MacBook Neo

Currently, the MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip. We expect it will get an upgrade to the A20 Pro chip that powers the iPad mini.

A larger iMac

Apple

Apple has launched the M6 iMac, but could there be something bigger coming? Reports suggest Apple has explored a new iMac Pro with a 32-inch mini-LED display. Pro-level performance is rumored, with more powerful chips and greater memory capacity than the standard model.

Read about the larger iMac rumors.

Should you buy now or wait?

With the prices of Macs increasing in June due to the global RAM shortages you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read the following for more guidance:

  • Should you buy the MacBook Pro now or wait?
  • Should you buy the MacBook Air now or wait?
  • Should you buy a Mac mini now or wait?
  • Should you buy a Mac Studio now or wait?

New AirPods coming in 2027

Apple

AirPods with a camera?

According to a brief update in Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter for Bloomberg in August, Apple is aiming to launch camera-equipped AirPods.

The new earbuds are expected to resemble the AirPods Pro 3, although it’s not yet clear whether they will also include a heart rate sensor.

The cameras are said to include both visible-light and infrared sensors, but they reportedly won’t be designed for taking photos or recording video, as their placement and image quality would make them unsuitable for those tasks. Instead, the cameras are expected to enable AI-powered features, such as hand gesture recognition, adapting audio based on the surrounding environment, and detecting whether someone is speaking directly to you or simply talking nearby.

Wondering whether to buy AirPods? Read Should I buy AirPods now and our AirPods buying guide.

Software updates

Apple released iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 and its other major updates in September 2026, introducing Siri AI, expanded Apple Intelligence features, new parental controls and app improvements. Further point updates will bring additional features, refinements and bug fixes.

For current features, availability and forthcoming additions, see our macOS 27 and iOS 27 guides. Our separate  latest iOS beta and latest macOS beta guides track testing of future updates.

Siri and Apple Intelligence

Siri AI brings more natural conversations, personal-context and onscreen awareness, and more actions across apps. Not every promised Siri AI feature was available at launch.

October’s 27.2 updates added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish alongside English. Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese are due by year-end. In the EU, Siri AI is available on macOS but remains unavailable on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS.

Availability depends on device, language and region, and some users may need to join a waiting list.

iOS 28, iPadOS 28, macOS 28

Apple is expected to preview its next major operating systems at WWDC in June 2027, followed by summer beta testing and public releases in the fall.

Apple smart-home products coming in 2027 and beyond

In October 2026 Apple announced a major expansion of its smart-home lineup with the launch of the HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection at its “Welcome Home” experience. We are still waiting for the update to the larger HomePod, with hope that could arrive in 2027.

Foundry

HomePod 3

  • Expected: 2027

The HomePod mini was updated in 2026, but not the larger HomePod. The reason for the delay may be that a more advanced HomePod speaker featuring a built-in display is coming.

HomeView Ultra

  • Possible release: 2027 or 2028, according to Bloomberg

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is developing a higher-end HomeView, codenamed J595, with a 9-inch display mounted on a motorized arm. The screen could rotate through 360 degrees and automatically turn toward whoever is speaking.

This would be a separate, more advanced model than the 7-inch HomeView announced in October 2026. Apple has not announced the device, and “HomeView Max” and “HomeView Ultra” remain speculative names. Read more about the HomeView Ultra here: ‘HomeView Ultra’ with robot arm may be coming next year

Upcoming Vision devices, AR and spatial computing

Apple Smart Glasses

  • Possible 2026 introduction, 2027 launch

Unlike the bulky Vision Pro headset, the upcoming smart glasses from Apple are expected to follow a form factor similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses. Said to be built specifically for “Visual Intelligence.” It will likely handle tasks such as live translations, music playback, phone calls, and turn-by-turn directions. Apple could provide a first glimpse or “preview” of the glasses by the end of 2026.

Vision Pro

  • Possible 2027 update

Prior to 2026, Apple’s spatial computing strategy has focused on the high-end market, but reports indicate a more affordable version of the headset is in development. Apple has reportedly paused work on a successor to the high-end Vision Pro and could instead release a cheaper Vision Pro.


What Apple launched in 2025

Here’s a quick look at what Apple released in 2025:

  • February 2025: iPhone 16E – the replacement for the iPhone SE and iPhone 14 brought Apple Intelligence support to the entry-level iPhone.
  • March 2025: iPad Air M3 and A16 iPad launched on March 4 and MacBook Air M4 and M4 Max Mac Studio on March 5.
  • September 2025: Apple introduced four new iPhones: iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, and the iPhone Air. We also saw the new AirPods Pro 3 and three new Apple Watches: the Series 11, Ultra 3 and SE 3.
  • October 2025: Apple announced a new M5 processor and released the M5 MacBook Pro, M5 iPad Pro, and an update to the Vision Pro, featuring the new chip.

What Apple launched in 2024

Here’s a quick look at what Apple released in 2024:

  • The Vision Pro headset arrived in the U.S. on February 2.
  • The M3 MacBook Air launched on March 4.
  • The M2 iPad Air, the M4 iPad Pro, and the Apple Pencil Pro all launched on May 7.
  • iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Plus launched on September 9.
  • iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro Max launched on September 9.
  • Apple Watch Series 10 launched on September 9.
  • AirPods 4 launched on September 9 and new colors (and USB-C) for the AirPods Max were introduced.
  • iPad mini A17 Pro launched on October 15.
  • Apple launched the M4 iMac, Mac mini, and MacBook Pro the week of October 28.

What Apple launched in 2023

Apple hit the ground running in 2023 and closed the year with the Vision Pro, although it didn’t arrive until 2024:

  • M2 Mac mini
  • Mac mini with M2 Pro
  • 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro with M2 Pro chip
  • New full size HomePod (bit of a surprise this one!)
  • A larger 15-inch MacBook Air
  • A new Mac Pro with the M2 Ultra
  • A new Mac Studio, also with M2 Ultra and M2 Max.
  • iPhone 15, Plus, Pro and Pro Max
  • 2023 Apple Watch Series 9 And Ultra 2
  • M3 iMac
  • M3, M3 Pro and M3 Max MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch)
  • And of course, the brand-new Vision Pro headset was unveiled
